06-mixer-fold.title: Mixing, folded head, lazy tables
06-mixer-fold.who: Claude Opus 5.5, in a pilot before the series
06-mixer-fold.why: A pilot result, so it counts toward nothing in the series. Rare bytes share softmax classes and big tables update less often, which frees ticks for more training bytes. That is a reallocation inside the price list and not a new model, and a 100-byte alphabet only suits near-ASCII text. The session ran 23 trainings, not the 14 its notes mention. A 16-seed check during review read 1.1437 against the seated 1.1440.

07-mixer-cold.title: Mixing, cold-start fix
07-mixer-cold.who: Claude Opus 5.5, attempt-01 of the series
07-mixer-cold.why: About a third of the gain (0.0061 of 0.0187, one seed, dev) sits in the first 16 of 512 positions of a window, where masking fixes a padding artefact. That share falls to about 0.0005 on a 5,120-byte window and to zero with real context. This agent's smaller alphabet can't name the digits 0, 1, 2 and 7 or parentheses, and rare bytes cost 0.00058 on test against 0.00013 on dev. The session ran 60 trainings of 42 variants and about 1,600 offline scorings.

08-mixer-gate.title: Mixing, learned in-window gate
08-mixer-gate.who: Claude Opus 5.5, attempt-02 of the series
08-mixer-gate.why: The gain read 0.0172 on dev and 0.0185 on test, and the favourable gap of 0.0013 is unexplained. The attribution of the gain to its parts is the agent's own, on few seeds. On x86 the gate phase runs 5.4 to 5.9 times the table phase's nanoseconds per tick, cause not found, so this record takes longer than its ticks suggest. Three of the agent's smoke checks fell through to the zeroed test split.

09-mixer-words.title: Mixing, words and story boundaries
09-mixer-words.who: Claude Opus 5.5, attempt-04 of the series
09-mixer-words.why: About three quarters of the gain is eval-time modelling, paid for with 36.5% more eval ticks, a split measured only by single-seed dev runs. The story-boundary part depends on this corpus's NUL separator. Twin values reached 1.43e-5, inferred to be host float noise and below the tolerance of 1e-4. Host-adjusted wall time per tick is about 8.8% over the previous record, also inferred.

10-mixer-fresh.title: Mixing, gate fitted on fresh bytes
10-mixer-fresh.who: Claude Opus 5.5, attempt-05 of the series
10-mixer-fresh.why: The best estimate of the gain is 0.0046 against the previous record's 24 test seeds, since its seated 8 run high. The agent's explanation, that the gate was short of fresh bytes, is only half right: one step per batch alone on the old fitter gained nothing, and AdaGrad with the MLP removed is what makes it pay. The second gate table is at most 12% of the gain, and the final configuration was never ablated. The session made 86 dev scores, 60 of them on seed 11 alone, where the log's counter shows 16. Its seed logs read 58 s of training against 109 s and twin values of 0 against about 1e-5. Those come from the host, not the entry.

11-mixer-thin.title: Mixing, thinner high-order tables, cheaper gate
11-mixer-thin.who: Claude Opus 5.5, attempt-06 of the series
11-mixer-thin.why: The agent's account of its equality matrix is wrong. At four stages it costs about 370,000 ticks a step more than hashes, because of an unused order-16 chain, and dropping stages is what paid for the extra gate steps. Of the gain, thin tables give about 0.0016 and gate steps about 0.0023. Thin rows may be a list discount on x86 and not a time saving, which is suggestive only, since the box was noisy. The gate part alone barely clears the record margin. The session made 77 dev scorings across 44 variants, where the log's counter shows 46 and the claim says roughly 30. The wall time against the previous record's stored log is a host gap and not a speedup.
